name: bias_add
summary: Out = Y + bias (broadcast on last dim). F16 half2(vec2) fastpath when N even + 4B aligned pointers.
contract: bias: rank==1, contiguous, same dtype as Y, shape[0]==N(last dim).
Out: same shape as Y, contiguous, same dtype as Y.
axis: only last dim allowed (-1 or rank-1).
abi: schema_id=='BADD' payload: int64 axis (little-endian, Python: struct.pack('<q', axis)).
notes: Launch config: kThreads=256, blocks=ceil(M*N/threads) capped to 65535.
Implementation computes MN by flattening all dims except last into M, last dim into N.
F16 vec2 path uses __half2 and requires 4B alignment for Y/bias/Out pointers.

variants.name: bias_add_f16_naive
variants.notes: Scalar half add using __hadd. Baseline for f16.

variants.name: bias_add_f16_vec2_half2
variants.notes: Vectorized half2 path using __hadd2. Improves throughput when eligible.

experiments.title: Add half2 fastpath (vec2)
experiments.change: Introduce bias_add_f16_vec2_half2 variant and eligibility checks: N even + 4B alignment.
experiments.why: Increase effective load/store throughput for f16 by processing 2 elements per thread op.
experiments.hypothesis: For large M*N and aligned memory, vec2 path increases GB/s and reduces latency vs f16_naive.
experiments.proof: Collect Nsight Compute: gld/gst throughput, achieved occupancy, memory throughput; confirm kernel name selection in logs.
experiments.next: Try wider vectorization (half4 via int2) or improve grid-stride with better launch bounds; consider 128 threads for L2-bound regimes.
